- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

- "CKA (Kornblith et al. 2019) — representation similarity context"

  - section: method
    word_budget: 750
    core_bullets:
      - "§3.1 Model Zoo: Wang et al. (2025) pretrained — 3 architectures (GatedDeltaNet, RetNet, HGRN2) × 5 attention ratios (0%, 4%, 7.7%, 14.3%, 25%) × 2 scales (340M, 1.3B); pure = 0% attention; h-k-1 = 1 attention layer per k+1 layers; transformer baseline"
      - "§3.2 Task Taxonomy (pre-defined, D003, NOT post-hoc): pure context retrieval = next-token prediction requiring long-range context without reasoning/knowledge (LAMBADA); comprehension = reading comprehension/QA (BoolQ); reasoning = commonsense/inference (HellaSwag, ARC-C, WinoGrande, PIQA, COPA); mixed = multiple skills (ARC-E, MMLU, SciQ, xstorycloze_en)"
      - "§3.3 Convergence Metrics: cross-arch std σ across 3 architectures at each attention ratio; Spearman ρ between attention ratio rank and σ; convergence ratio = σ_pure / σ_{h3-1}"
      - "§3.4 Per-Example Decomposition: helped = acc_hybrid > acc_pure; hurt = acc_hybrid < acc_pure; net effect = helped - hurt; pairwise Jaccard J = |A∩B| / |A∪B| across architecture pairs"
      - "§3.5 Statistical Methods: exact permutation test (n=5, 120 perms, two-tailed); BCa bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, architecture-level); Bonferroni correction (6 benchmarks pre-registered D003); Mann-Whitney U for within-arch comparisons; Kruskal-Wallis for cross-arch comparisons"
    dependencies: []
    notation_table:
      σ: "cross-architecture standard deviation"
      ρ: "Spearman rank correlation"
      J: "pairwise Jaccard similarity"
      h-k-1: "hybrid with 1 attention layer per k+1 total layers (e.g., h3-1 = 25% attention)"
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-008]

  - section: experiments
    word_budget: 1800
    core_bullets:
      - "§4.1 Task-Specific Convergence (C1): Table 1 shows 10 benchmarks; only LAMBADA has ρ=-1.0 (p=0.017 exact perm); BCa CI [-1.0, -0.7]; σ drops 0.024→0.005 (79%); Bonferroni adj-p=0.100 'does not survive strict correction'; task-specificity IS the finding — LAMBADA uniquely tests pure context retrieval; Figure 2 forest plot visualizes"
      - "§4.2 Scale-Dependent Convergence (C2): 1.3B monotonically converges (ρ=-1.0); 340M partial convergence (56% σ reduction but non-monotonic rebound at h3-1); binary contrast — scale is necessary condition for complete equalization; two data points, NOT a scalable trend"
      - "§4.3 Per-Example Divergence (C3a): Table 2 — pairwise Jaccard < 0.10 for all architecture pairs; GDN net -153, HGRN2 net +153, RetNet net -69; surface features do NOT differentiate helped/hurt within arch (exp-003 negative); BUT cross-arch Kruskal-Wallis p=0.0005 for hurt samples → architecture-specificity is structured, not random"
      - "§4.4 Decoupling (C3b, title-level contribution): Figure 1 — aggregate σ decreases gradually (0.024→0.016→0.014→0.006→0.005) across 5 attention levels; Jaccard saturates at first level (4%→~0.095) and stays flat; net asymmetry increases (0.013→0.040); aggregate convergence and per-example divergence operate on different timescales = decoupling. Attention weight analysis (exp-004-r2): GDN↔RetNet L2 cosine=0.995 yet per-example effects differ → divergence not in attention layer but in recurrent layers; HGRN2↔others cosine~0.20 in early layers, converges >0.94 at L20. 1-2 sentences in text, full 8-layer × 3-pair data in Appendix D."
      - "§4.5 Robustness (brief, details in appendix): GDN-excluded sensitivity — LAMBADA ρ→-0.7 (p=0.233), MMLU flips +0.6 (D007); BCa degenerate resamples 11.25% formally justified"
    dependencies: [method]
    tables: [tab1_convergence, tab2_per_example]
    figures: [fig2_task_specificity]
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-003, exp-003-p2, exp-004-r2, exp-008, exp-009, exp-010, exp-011, exp-011-xstorycloze, eval_340m_retnet_hgrn2]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 350
    core_bullets:
      - "Summary: first systematic per-example analysis of attention's equalizing effect in hybrid recurrent architectures — decoupling is title-level contribution"
      - "Key findings recap: (1) task-specific convergence on LAMBADA only, (2) scale-dependent (1.3B complete, 340M partial), (3) aggregate convergence and per-example divergence decoupled"
      - "Practical implication: architecture selection based on aggregate benchmarks may mask per-example behavioral differences that matter for deployment"
      - "Future work: interventional experiments (attention head ablation/swaps); scaling beyond 1.3B; other hybrid families (Jamba, RWKV-6); fine-tuning analysis"
    dependencies: [experiments]
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-010]

  - section: limitations
    word_budget: 300
    core_bullets:
      - "n=5 attention ratios: minimum achievable p≈0.008, statistical power inherently limited"
      - "LAMBADA-only per-example analysis: sample-level decomposition requires significant convergence benchmark"
      - "Two scale points (340M, 1.3B): binary contrast, not scalable trend; 7B+ unavailable"
      - "Three architectures (GDN, RetNet, HGRN2): more families needed to generalize"
      - "Descriptive, not causal: attention weight analysis is observational; interventional experiments = future work"
      - "Pre-trained only: no fine-tuning or downstream task adaptation analysis"
    dependencies: [experiments]

      This is the paper's title-level contribution.

      - "Right-side inline text: ρ value and p value for each benchmark"
      - "COPA row marked with dagger (supplementary, n=100)"
      - "Taxonomy labels on right margin or as row grouping"
    data_source: "artifacts/paper_data/convergence_table.csv"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "3:4"

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.labelsize': 12,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.05,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
    'lines.linewidth': 1.8,
})

# --- Data ---
attn_ratios_a = [0, 4, 7.7, 14.3, 25]
sigma_1_3B =    [0.02405, 0.01624, 0.01360, 0.00606, 0.00494]
sigma_340M =    [0.0246,  0.0109,  0.0173,  0.0108,  0.0151]

attn_ratios_b = [4, 7.7, 14.3, 25]
j_helped =      [0.0945, 0.0951, 0.0922, 0.1002]
j_hurt =        [0.0873, 0.0809, 0.0988, 0.0928]

# --- Colors ---
color_1_3B = '#0072B2'
color_340M = '#999999'
color_jaccard = '#555555'

# --- Figure ---
fig, (ax_a, ax_b) = plt.subplots(
    1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.5),
    gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [1.3, 1], 'wspace': 0.35}
)

# ============ Panel (a): Cross-architecture sigma ============
ax_a.plot(attn_ratios_a, sigma_1_3B, '-o', color=color_1_3B,
          linewidth=2.2, markersize=7, label='1.3B', zorder=3)
ax_a.plot(attn_ratios_a, sigma_340M, '--^', color=color_340M,
          linewidth=1.2, markersize=6, label='340M', zorder=3)

# Annotation: -79% on 1.3B endpoint
drop_pct = (sigma_1_3B[-1] - sigma_1_3B[0]) / sigma_1_3B[0] * 100
t = ax_a.annotate(
    f'{drop_pct:.0f}%',
    xy=(attn_ratios_a[-1], sigma_1_3B[-1]),
    xytext=(attn_ratios_a[-1] - 5, sigma_1_3B[-1] + 0.005),
    fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', color=color_1_3B,
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color_1_3B, lw=1.2),
    zorder=4
)
t.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2.5, foreground='white')])

# Annotation: 340M non-monotonic rebound
rebound_idx = 2  # 7.7% has a bump
t2 = ax_a.annotate(
    'rebound',
    xy=(attn_ratios_a[rebound_idx], sigma_340M[rebound_idx]),
    xytext=(attn_ratios_a[rebound_idx] + 3, sigma_340M[rebound_idx] + 0.005),
    fontsize=8, fontstyle='italic', color=color_340M,
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color_340M, lw=0.8),
    zorder=4
)
t2.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2.5, foreground='white')])

ax_a.set_xlabel('Attention ratio (%)')
ax_a.set_ylabel(r'Cross-architecture $\sigma$')
ax_a.set_xticks(attn_ratios_a)
ax_a.set_xticklabels(['0', '4', '7.7', '14.3', '25'])
ax_a.set_ylim(0, 0.030)
ax_a.legend(loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)

# Panel subtitle (insight)
t_sub = ax_a.set_title('(a) Gradual reduction across 5 levels',
                        fontsize=10, fontstyle='italic', pad=8)

# ============ Panel (b): Pairwise Jaccard ============

# Saturation band (Pattern A)
ax_b.axhspan(0.085, 0.105, color='#E0E0E0', alpha=0.35, zorder=0)
t_band = ax_b.text(25.3, 0.070, 'saturation zone', fontsize=7.5,
                    color='#aaaaaa', fontstyle='italic', ha='right', va='center')
t_band.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2, foreground='white')])

ax_b.plot(attn_ratios_b, j_helped, '-o', color=color_jaccard,
          linewidth=1.8, markersize=7, label='J(helped)', zorder=3)
ax_b.plot(attn_ratios_b, j_hurt, '--D', color=color_jaccard,
          linewidth=1.4, markersize=6, markerfacecolor='white',
          markeredgecolor=color_jaccard, markeredgewidth=1.3,
          label='J(hurt)', zorder=3)

# Annotation: "saturates at 4%"
t3 = ax_b.annotate(
    'saturates at 4%',
    xy=(attn_ratios_b[0], j_helped[0]),
    xytext=(attn_ratios_b[0] + 5, j_helped[0] + 0.015),
    fontsize=9, fontstyle='italic', color='#333333',
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#333333', lw=0.8),
    zorder=4
)
t3.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2.5, foreground='white')])

ax_b.set_xlabel('Attention ratio (%)')
ax_b.set_ylabel('Pairwise Jaccard similarity')
ax_b.set_xticks(attn_ratios_b)
ax_b.set_xticklabels(['4', '7.7', '14.3', '25'])
ax_b.set_ylim(0.065, 0.120)
ax_b.legend(loc='lower right', framealpha=0.9)

# Panel subtitle (insight)
ax_b.set_title('(b) Immediate saturation at first level',
               fontsize=10, fontstyle='italic', pad=8)

# --- Save ---
import os
out_dir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_2/projects/entrainment_gated_ft/figures/paper'
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

pdf_path = os.path.join(out_dir, 'fig1_decoupling_hero.pdf')
png_path = os.path.join(out_dir, 'fig1_decoupling_hero.png')

fig.savefig(png_path, dpi=300)

print(f'Saved: {pdf_path}')
